citations.assessment: The same Mishnah puts Eliezer ben Yaakov’s account of the platform alongside Abba Yose ben Chanan’s statement about the gates.
The baraita names Abba Yose ben Yochanan of Jerusalem transmitting from Rabbi Meir. The ensuing discussion reads ben Chanan. Retain both received forms in editorial evidence.
The dedicated Jerusalem headword explicitly distinguishes the separate Abba Yose entry. Follow the pointer without identifying the individuals.
The internal article quotes the Pesachim and Tosefta variants. Checked Pesachim gives a transmission from Abba Yosef ben Chanin, while Tosefta juxtaposes the two names with a longer patronymic.
The witness gives Abba Yose ben Chanan of Yanuach in the name of Abba Kohen ben Delaya. Midrash Tannaim gives the longer ben Yochanan and bar Delaya forms. Keep Heilprin’s Bardela.
All three names occur in the baraita on how long merit can defer the consequence of the ordeal.
The parallel gives Yosef ben Chanan followed by Elazar ben Yitzchak and Rabbi Yishmael.

holds.reason: The named passage did not surface in the checked Mishnah Eduyot chapter text. The folio may reflect an edition, commentary or different locator.
Both named sages occur in the cited Middot mishnah. This supports the provisional expansion of the siglum and leaves the chronological inference qualified.
